note: 006 Empire State Building, 'built in 410 days'. Structure: narrator (F, Jessica, opens + explains) + interrupting sceptic (M, Eric, hunts for 'the catch', carries the jokes). Voices 006 per rotation: Eric + Jessica.
lines: They built the Empire State Building in 410 days.
They built the EMPIRE STATE BUILDING in 410 DAYS.
410 days? My phone contract lasts longer than that.
410 DAYS? My PHONE CONTRACT lasts longer than that.
102 floors, in just over a year. And the very top was built for something that never worked.
102 FLOORS, in just over a YEAR. And the very TOP was built for something that NEVER worked.
No catch. Just a clever system. The steel arrived cut and labelled, like flat-pack furniture.
No catch. Just a clever SYSTEM. The steel arrived CUT and LABELLED, like FLAT-PACK furniture.
Flat-pack? Mine always comes with one screw missing.
FLAT-PACK? Mine always comes with ONE SCREW missing.
Theirs was 57,000 tons of steel. And little railway carts on every floor zipped it to the crews.
Theirs was 57,000 TONS of steel. And little RAILWAY CARTS on every floor zipped it to the crews.
And the frame climbed four and a half floors a week.
And the frame climbed FOUR AND A HALF FLOORS a WEEK.
Four and a half floors? I can't answer four and a half emails a week.
FOUR AND A HALF FLOORS? I can't answer FOUR AND A HALF EMAILS a week.
Fine, it's impressive. So what never worked?
Fine, it's IMPRESSIVE. So what NEVER worked?
The tip. That spire was designed as a parking spot for airships.
The TIP. That SPIRE was designed as a PARKING SPOT for AIRSHIPS.
Passengers would step off, over 1,000 feet up. But the wind had other ideas.
Passengers would STEP OFF, over 1,000 FEET up. But the WIND had other ideas.
Did anyone ever actually park there?
Did anyone ever actually PARK there?
One small airship, in 1931. For about three minutes.
One small AIRSHIP, in 1931. For about THREE MINUTES.
[laughs] So, 410 days to build it, and three minutes of parking.
So, 410 DAYS to build it, and THREE MINUTES of parking.
